Except for the occasional B-ultrasound examination, pregnant moms cannot understand the status of their babies living in the womb through their eyes. Just like mothers use facial expressions to judge their children's needs and problems, pregnant moms need to monitor the safety of their baby in the womb through fetal movements. If the fetal movement is abnormal, it is likely that there is intrauterine hypoxia in the fetus. Fetal movement decreases until it disappears within 24 hours, the fetal heart rate will disappear.
